paper_metadata.title: Towards An End-To-End Approach For Quantum Principal Component Analysis

summary: The paper implements an end‑to‑end Quantum PCA workflow using phase estimation and a custom tomography method to reconstruct eigenvectors, demonstrated on a 2×2 synthetic covariance matrix using r_PE=2 qubits and Nc=50,000 shots. Circuits use 4 qubits for phase estimation and 5 qubits for the sign‑estimation tomography step, tested on the IBM qasm simulator and an IBM Perth (7‑qubit, quantum volume 32) device. Results correctly identify eigenvalues (~0.75 and ~0.25 due to 2‑bit resolution) but hardware runs suffer from decoherence in the deeper sign‑estimation circuit.

experiments.description: Quantum PCA on a 2x2 synthetic covariance matrix for an interest-rate-risk use case, using phase estimation to estimate eigenvalues and a tomography-based sign estimation circuit to reconstruct principal components; evaluated on IBM ideal simulator and IBM Perth QPU.

algorithm.variant: Quantum PCA with phase estimation and extended quantum state tomography

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Input covariance matrix A is amplitude-encoded into register M; phase estimation uses register E with r_PE qubits to encode eigenvalues; sign estimation adds one control qubit.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Extract principal components (eigenvalues and eigenvectors) of the input covariance matrix via quantum PCA.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: e^{-iAt} used for phase estimation / Hamiltonian simulation

problem_instance.description: Interest rate risk / financial covariance-matrix PCA on synthetic 2-asset data.

dataset_specification.description: 2x2 synthetic covariance matrix validated by domain experts; matrix A = [[0.6507, 0.2122],[0.2122, 0.3493]] with eigenvalues 0.760 and 0.240 and eigenvectors [0.889, 0.459] and [-0.459, 0.889].

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Daily computed differences among tenors are modeled with ARMA, cleaned from outliers, and PCA is applied to residuals in the motivating finance workflow; for the experiment, a synthetic covariance matrix is generated from simulated returns.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Ideal simulation on ibmq qasm simulator with 50000 shots; additional runs on IBM Perth QPU; results compared qualitatively against expected eigenvalues/signs.

hardware.device_name: ibmq_qasm_simulator (ideal simulator) and IBM Perth QPU

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Matrix normalization by trace if needed; synthetic covariance matrix generation from simulated returns.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Eigenvalues multiplied by trace if normalization was applied; principal components reconstructed from tomography output.

results.value: 1000 simulated scenarios per asset over one year

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical PCA / classical linear algebra methods
speedup_claims.conditions: for low-rank density matrices in the original quantum PCA proposal; this paper does not empirically demonstrate the advantage
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper discusses the theoretical quantum PCA advantage from prior work, but does not provide a direct classical runtime comparison for the reported experiment.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(t^2 ε^-1 log(N^2)) for Hamiltonian simulation / phase estimation; tomography adds O((36 d ln d / δ^2) t^2 ε^-1 log(N^2))

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not provided; experiment only demonstrates a 2x2 covariance matrix.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Requires scalable qRAM-based data loading and large coherent phase estimation registers for meaningful matrices.
limiting_factors: Eigenvalue estimation resolution limited to r_PE = 2 qubits
Heavy reliance on state preparation (placeholder instead of qRAM)

notes: IBM ideal simulator and IBM Perth QPU are explicitly reported; 5 qubits comes from 2 qubits for register M + 2 for register E + 1 control qubit in sign estimation.
Circuit depth is not numerically reported; left null.
The paper gives asymptotic quantum complexity but does not provide a classical baseline complexity for the same task, so speedup order is set to none_proven.
The paper references theoretical exponential advantage from Lloyd et al. (2014) quantum PCA but does not empirically demonstrate any runtime improvement.
Experiments are limited to a 2x2 matrix on an ideal simulator.

experiments.description: Execution of the same Quantum PCA circuits (phase estimation and sign estimation tomography circuits) on a real IBM Perth superconducting quantum processor to evaluate hardware behavior versus ideal simulation.

algorithm.variant: Quantum PCA with phase estimation and extended tomography
key_components: Sign estimation circuit using Hadamard-test-like construction

key_results: Amplitude estimation results on hardware are reasonably close to ideal simulator results.
Sign estimation circuit degrades significantly on hardware due to increased circuit depth and decoherence.
